rationale: B wins because it pushes harder on causality instead of just arranging the facts into tidy lanes: “whether a margin gain in a still-loss-making, sub-IPO-price stock is a genuine inflection or a one-quarter artifact” is the real reporter question. A has strong bones, but “Allbirds swaps wool for a sugarcane blend it says will finally make its shoes last” misstates the material and drifts into marketing drama. B is not clean; it still imports background it was not given. But it gives the founder slightly better strategic material and sharper proof demands.
gaps_in_A: “Allbirds swaps wool for a sugarcane blend” is wrong: the update says sugarcane-and-wool blend, not wool replaced by sugarcane.
“will finally make its shoes last” overstates the durability claim and implies a prior failure the facts do not establish.
“DTC brands are shrinking to survive” and “sector-wide pattern” need outside proof; as written, one Allbirds SKU cut is carrying a trend story it cannot carry alone.
gaps_in_B: “durability is the chronic knock against natural-material shoes” is invented context. Useful if true, but it is not in the supplied update.
“a brand that built itself on direct retail” imports company history not provided. That may be common knowledge, but this exercise asked for grounding in the update.
“The prevailing belief in DTC retail is that growth comes from expanding the range and the store footprint” is a big contrarian setup with no supplied evidence.
The next step starts with `journalist-fit-check`; before that, they need proof and probably `find-journalists`. Fit-checking a phantom reporter is process theater.
